rationale: Lycopolitan ⲡⲕⲉⲥ = Sahidic ⲕⲁⲥ 'bone.' First member of the five-element body system in the Kephalaia anthropology (bone/sinew/vein/flesh/skin), correlated to mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection respectively.
Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲧ = 'sinew, nerve.' Second of the five body elements; correlated to thought.
Coptic ⲙⲟⲟⲙⲉ = 'vein, vessel.' Third of the five body elements; correlated to teaching.
Coptic ϣⲁⲁⲣ/ϣⲁⲣⲉ = 'skin, hide.' Fifth of the five body elements; correlated to reflection.

Compound: ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ ('new'). Standard Manichaean term for the regenerated soul-body that the Savior fashions, son of Righteousness, with five living members corresponding to love, faith, perfection (and presumably two more in the lacuna). Equivalent to Pauline καινὸς ἄνθρωπος adopted into Manichaean technical vocabulary.

ϫⲱⲕ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ literally 'completion outward' — to bring to fullness, accomplish. As the noun-virtue identified with the teaching-faculty of the New Man, 'perfection' captures the technical sense (cf. Greek τελείωσις).
Lycopolitan form of Sahidic ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'faith, trust, belief.' Identified here with the thought-faculty of the New Man.

Most likely from ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, stamp, mold,' with light verb ⲣ̄- ('do, make'). 'She stamps her substance and her kind and her form' — Sin imprints her character upon her own essence-categories. Alternative: ⲧⲱⲃⲉ also = 'requite, recompense,' but that fits less well here. Reading remains uncertain; flagged in footnote.

Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲱⲩⲗⲏⲩ, tentatively read as a verbal noun from a root meaning 'go up, ascend' (cf. ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲉ, ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲥ). Sin does not know 'the door of the place of ascent' — the way out and up. The reading is tentative.
